items.title: Hinton Milt — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: He got a Pullman car to come pull us up and got us to some place, put the car on the side track and kept the Pullman for like two or three months, same guy and he [unintelligible] the car.

ctx.x: Yeah, looking good, really together. We traveled right across the country like that on the way to California. We got to California. We played the theater out there, we played the Million Dollar [Unintelligible]. Now we‟ve got to come back. Now we‟ve played everything in California, now we‟ve got to come back to one-nighters. That‟s where it gets tough, coming back to one- nighters because you can‟t take… the trains don‟t go to all those little one [unintelligible] so we‟ve got to take the bus. Now that‟s kind of…

Everybody was poor, blacks and whites, everybody was poor, had nothing, just nothing. The white people who owned most of the property were getting disgusted because there was so much oil…
